question: How do the two small boats look? Alex (decision water-layer): 'We need at least one small boat. Maybe two?', then 'Correct, part of the environment with real patrols but no specific part in the mission'.
source: scripts/ui/boards/boats_board_shot.gd: the new generators in scripts/render/boat_art.gd (the unit sheet's style), framed by scripts/render/boat_frame.gd on Track WB's proposed water, one InkCanvas per frame; no sandbox is stood up and nothing in the game changes

held_constant.light: the map's sun (data/params/render_defaults.json: from the north-west, elevation 46, shadow strength 0.44), so a boat's shadow falls south-east
held_constant.pen: the game's own pen (render_defaults linework.pen, shadow side); outlines heavy on the faces away from the sun
held_constant.water: Track WB's PROPOSED default water, read at render time from data/world/water.json draw.palette (the shelf step; shallows and deep in the depth strip), flat; Track WB's board (variants/water/) decides the water. Falls back to a placeholder wash when that file is absent
held_constant.what_they_are: real units on a patrol route with no part in the mission (Alex); the patrol boat's guns are drawn trained and stowed, no fire
held_constant.sides: side_a brick red above, side_b slate blue below: one accent zone each (a painted recognition panel)
held_constant.plane_beside: the light fighter (9 m) at 400 m, drawn by the game's own unit_marker_art, its shadow offset by its altitude

scale_rule_proposed.source: data/ui/ui.json marker.true_scale as scripts/app/sandbox.gd _update_plane_scale sets it: plane_px 36 and plane_min_px 14 (data/scenarios/strike.json view) over the light fighter's 9 m and the map's 2 px per metre

palette_check: No option adds a hue. Fills are the paper ramp (roof_lit, wall_fill, object_fill: L 0.922, 0.880, 0.925), shaded halves the one mix toward the shadow tint, material is linework; the side accents (side_a L 0.551 C 0.100, side_b L 0.551 C 0.100) sit on ONE zone per boat. The placeholder water is the one exception and is Track WB's to decide.
recommendation_proposed: PROPOSED by Track BB, Alex decides: patrol P1 (the cutter) and supply S1 (the coaster) -- the two that read as a warship and as a cargo boat at both zooms -- at the planes' scale (the plane rule), with the PALE WASH for the wake if one wake has to serve both zooms (it is the only one that still says moving at 0.35), or the ink V if the wake must add no tone at all. P3 is the cheap fallback for the patrol boat (almost the same at the planning zoom) and S2 the supply boat that reads as cargo from furthest away. On Track WB's lightest step (the shallows) a hull is held by its outline and shadow more than its fill: worth a look when WB settles the water.
